Ana Carter: heads-up — ran a synthetic canary against the new edge-allocator yesterday and saw a fairness imbalance. one tenant (acct: atlas-inc) consumed ~2x credits compared to previous runs, despite same QPS.
Mike Huang: ugh. can you paste the raw metrics? was KV cache hit-rate different?
Ana Carter: attaching quick excerpt from the run (trimmed).
Ana Carter: ```
tenant=atlas-inc credits_used=12000
tenant=atlas-inc average_latency_ms=43
tenant=control-group credits_used=6100
kv_cache_hits=0.12
edge_reconcile_errors=3
```
Sasha Iqbal: kv_cache_hits that low is suspicious. were we routing to a quantized variant during the test? that could change token accounting.
Ana Carter: no quantized swap. routing table shows same model version. I think the ledger reconciliation window is the culprit — edge counters were allowed to overspend before central ledger corrected.
Lee Patel: that maps to a long-standing race: edge reports -> central aggregates -> credit deduction. if the reconcile window is wide, edges keep serving using provisional credits.
Mike Huang: agreed. tradeoff was intentional to keep tail latency low. but we didn't simulate a sustained burst where many edges overspend in parallel.
Sasha Iqbal: we need to decide on a surface: do we tighten the provisional credit window, or add a token-level soft cap that stalls requests once per-tenant provisional usage exceeds X%? both have perf implications.
Ana Carter: proposal A: reduce reconcile_window_ms from 5s -> 1s and enable immediate delta pushes on hot-tenants.
Mike Huang: proposal B: keep window but add local soft_shed threshold: if provisional_usage > 1.25 * reserved_quota then start shedding low-priority calls (rerank/embeddings).
Lee Patel: both are viable. A reduces the inconsistency surface but increases control-plane load. B keeps control-plane load low but adds behavioral complexity in edge.
Sasha Iqbal: operationally, B gives us more gradual degradation and preserves overall throughput. A might cause oscillation if many edges hammer the control plane simultaneously.
Mike Huang: quick config sketch for B: ```json
{"soft_shed_ratio":1.25, "soft_shed_actions":["deprioritize-rerank","delay-embeddings-50ms"], "probe_mode": true}```
Ana Carter: important to add observability: we need per-tenant provisional vs committed metrics, and a small audit log for every soft_shed decision. right now our dashboards only show post-reconcile committed credits.
Lee Patel: +1. I can wire provisional metrics into the Console telemetry. timeline: 1) add metrics 2) implement soft_shed 3) run shadowing canaries 4) flip on.
Sasha Iqbal: also raise the question of rollback semantics for Dedicated customers — they expect stronger isolation. soft_shed must respect reserved capacity and never apply to SLA-backed tenants.
Mike Huang: good call. soft_shed config should include an allowlist and a strict SLA flag. default for SLA=true -> bypass soft_shed.
Ana Carter: action items: 1) Mike -> open PR with soft_shed sketch + unit tests (due EOD Thu). 2) Lee -> add provisional/committed metrics to console (ETA Fri). 3) Sasha -> write an ops playbook for probe_mode canary + rollback conditions (ETA Mon). 4) Ops -> run burst sim with atlas-inc pattern once metrics are in.
